taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes Feist et al. (2019) suggested mtDNA evidence for two lineages within P. websteri; formerly confused with the P. dorsalis group.
fieldMarks: Small woodland salamander, 2.75-3.2 in (7.0-8.2 cm); striped form has a wavy yellowish-brown to orange-red stripe head to tail; unstriped form may have scattered red pigment.
Tiny silvery-white spots and brassy flecks give a frosted look.
Belly mottled orange or reddish; males have a swollen cloaca.
behavior: Active in forest litter roughly October-May and apparently inactive underground in other months.
Terrestrial breeder: courtship January-March, eggs laid June-July, hatching August-September.
Some populations move to rocky outcrops in spring and leave them in fall.
habitat: Hardwood or mixed pine-hardwood forested hillsides, often bordering rocky feeder streams; under rocks, logs, bark and leaf litter.
range: Small, scattered populations in the southeastern Piedmont and adjacent areas: western South Carolina, west Georgia, central and east-central Alabama, south-central Mississippi and Louisiana. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Southern zigzag salamander
lookalikes.howToTell: Nearly identical; best separated by geographic distribution and genetics.

lookalikes.name: Southern redback salamander (Plethodon serratus)
lookalikes.howToTell: Where ranges overlap in western Georgia, redback has a straighter stripe with serrated edges; Webster's stripe is more jagged.
